raw_response.publication_year_note: Both the journal volume/issue header (Water International, 2024, Vol. 49, No. 5, pp. 641-663) and the online publication date (Published online: 03 Jun 2024; Accepted 3 May 2024) are in 2024.
raw_response.rationale: Full text read (24 pages). The study describes a pilot university-government collaboration in Boloso Sore woreda, Wolaita Zone, Ethiopia that conducted a GPS census of 121 shallow-well water schemes (112 shallow wells and 9 shallow boreholes) and encoded them into an Excel/ArcGIS database. Empirical outputs consist exclusively of descriptive counts, functionality percentages (e.g., 13.2% [n = 15] non-functional shallow wells and 44.5% [n = 4/9] non-functional shallow boreholes, PDF pp. 14-16), management shares (97.5% [n = 116] community-managed, PDF p. 16), and rule-of-thumb coverage percentages derived by multiplying functional schemes by national standard capacities (Tables 2 and 3, PDF pp. 18-19). No inferential statistics, regressions, hypothesis tests, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported anywhere in the paper, and the discussed mandatory data-reporting requirement for NGOs had not yet been enacted. Flagging quantitative synthesis eligibility is therefore overstated.
